name: input.send_message
description: Synchronous Win32 `SendMessage` escape hatch. Posts the message and waits for the target's wndproc to return; the LRESULT is returned in the response body.

msg.description: Win32 message identifier (e.g. `0x0010` for WM_CLOSE, `0x000E` for WM_GETTEXTLENGTH). The bridge accepts hex strings (`"0x0010"`) and decimal.

wparam.description: Message-specific WPARAM. Signed 64-bit. The bridge accepts hex strings.

lparam.description: Message-specific LPARAM. Signed 64-bit. The bridge accepts hex strings.

lresult.description: LRESULT returned by SendMessage. Interpretation is message-specific — refer to Win32 docs for the relevant WM_* or app-defined message. Signed 64-bit on x64.

x-implementations.name: send_message
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendMessageW`. Blocks the agent's request thread until the target's wndproc returns. If the target is unresponsive, prefer `input.post_message` to avoid agent stalls.

windows-modern.description: SendMessageW. UIPI: cross-IL sends are silently no-op'd by the OS (no error returned by SendMessage itself); agent post-checks via GetWindowThreadProcessId / integrity comparison and returns ERR uipi_blocked when the IL barrier blocks delivery. Long-running wndprocs can stall the request thread; agent applies a configurable timeout (defaults to 5s) and returns ERR timeout if exceeded.

windows-classic.description: SendMessageW (NT 5+) or SendMessageA (NT 4 / 9x, with input transcoding from UTF-8 wparam/lparam strings). No UIPI on classic — sends cross all process boundaries.
